summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of idiopathic gastroparesis and J-tube placement was admitted for a flare characterized by sudden abdominal pain and vomiting during a tube feed. She had no signs of infection, obstruction, or metabolic instability. Treatment included IV fluids, antiemetics (ondansetron, prochlorperazine), Ativan, and morphine, with gradual reintroduction of tube feeds. She tolerated full feeds at 90 mL/hr and remained symptom-free, leading to discharge home after two days. Her hypothyroidism was stable on levothyroxine, and all other chronic conditions were managed without change. Follow-up was arranged with her gastroenterologist.
